meta.name: Scarlet Inspector
meta.tagline: Every WebSocket frame, captured and inspectable.
meta.summary: A drop-in Scarlet WebSocket decorator for Android: it records every frame into Room and exposes sessions in a Compose inspector launched from a persistent notification. Built as a reusable library with a deliberately thin sample host.
meta.role: Solo Android engineer — library design, Compose UI, Room persistence, benchmark integration

story.headline: An inspector for the invisible half of Android networking.
story.problem: WebSocket traffic is the hardest part of an Android app to debug: frames fly past, sessions blend together, and logcat gives you a wall of text with no notion of a session. Existing HTTP inspectors stop at request/response — they do not understand long-lived sockets.
story.approach: Mirror the decorator idea onto Scarlet: a WebSocketFactory wrapper and a WebSocket decorator record each frame into Room, tag it with a session identity resolved by a tracker, and surface the result through a foreground-service notification that opens a Compose UI. The library keeps a four-file public surface so internals stay free to change, and skips DI frameworks entirely — constructor parameters instead.
story.outcome: The sample host runs two Scarlet clients against one endpoint and the inspector captures both into separate sessions, with frames replayable in a list → detail flow from the notification. The app then became the benchmark target for my research on JEV decision hooks — fifteen refactor tasks across ten rule areas.

layers.name: Inspection UI
layers.description: Compose screens launched from the notification.

components.name: Inspector UI
components.summary: The inspection surface, launched from the notification.
components.description: Hosts the Compose tree; receives the launcher intent and owns navigation between list and detail.

components.name: List screen
components.description: Renders recorded sessions with type and frame counts; selecting one opens the frame list.

components.name: Detail screen
components.summary: Every frame in a session, in order.
components.description: Shows sent and received frames with direction and payload preview; long sessions scroll through frame rows.

components.name: Frame row
components.description: Direction badge, timestamp, truncated payload; a compact row that keeps long sessions scannable.

layers.name: Delivery & lifecycle
layers.description: What keeps inspection alive outside the foreground.

components.name: Inspector core
components.summary: Entry point — one object holds the DB and the IO scope.
components.description: Creates the Room database, owns the SupervisorJob IO scope, and exposes clearAllData(); everything else hangs off it.

components.name: Inspector svc
components.summary: Keeps inspection alive while the app is backgrounded.
components.description: Foreground service that owns the notification and the inspection lifecycle.

components.name: Notification
components.summary: The permanent doorway into the inspector.
components.description: Persistent notification; tapping it launches the UI from anywhere in the app.

components.name: Launcher
components.summary: Turns a notification tap into a Compose screen.
components.description: Public helper that resolves the intent and starts the inspector activity.

layers.name: Capture
layers.description: Where frames are intercepted and tagged.

components.name: Factory wrap
components.description: The install point: returns decorated WebSockets instead of raw OkHttp-backed ones, without touching client code.

components.name: Socket wrap
components.summary: Records every frame as it passes.
components.description: Delegates open(), wraps the event stream, and writes sent and received frames to the active session.

components.name: Session tags
components.description: Resolves and reuses session ids so two clients against one endpoint — or a reconnect — stay distinguishable.

components.name: InspectorDao
components.description: Suspend functions for insert, read and clear; the only thing the capture layer and the UI are allowed to touch.

components.name: Room store
components.summary: Sessions and frames that survive process death.
components.description: Room database with SocketSession and SocketFrame entities; the reason this beats logcat is that the history is still there tomorrow.

layers.name: Sample host
layers.description: The smallest possible integration, kept deliberately thin.

components.name: MainActivity
components.summary: The thin host that proves the library.
components.description: Wires two Scarlet clients, connect/disconnect/send controls, and installs the inspector.

components.name: Financial API
components.description: Sends subscribe payloads and receives protobuf channel messages as a Flow — representative app traffic to debug.

components.name: Stream adapter
components.summary: Glue between Scarlet streams and Kotlin Flow.
components.description: Bridges the library's stream types so the sample reads like ordinary coroutine code.

flows.label: Frames in
flows.description: An app message leaves the host, passes through the decorators, and lands in Room.

flows.label: Frames out
flows.description: The notification opens the inspector; list and detail read the same rows Room stored.
